translation: Pallavi (Chorus): Son-in-law: O mother-in-law, your daughter puts me through an ordeal like Rama's... what can I say... Mother-in-law, O mother-in-law, your daughter... she's a whole basket of nagging, O mother-in-law... she's a whole basket of quarrels, my mother-in-law...
Mother-in-law: What is it, son-in-law, what's the matter... why are you saying such things, what's the matter... why are you saying such things, what's the matter...

Son-in-law: She finds fault with everything, O mother-in-law... she won't do even this much work, my mother-in-law... Mother-in-law: With a big strapping fellow like you around, O son-in-law... why would she do the work, O son-in-law...

(Mother-in-law, O mother-in-law, your daughter is a whole basket of nagging, O mother-in-law, she's a whole basket of quarrels, my mother-in-law) (What is it, son-in-law, what's the matter, why are you saying such things, what's the matter, why are you saying such things, what's the matter)

Verse 1: Son-in-law: O mother-in-law... she wanders from this house to that house and tells me to scrub the dishes, O mother-in-law... tells me to sweep the front yard, O mother-in-law... Mother-in-law: Ever since she was little, O son-in-law... she never did even a small chore, O son-in-law... my daughter grew up like a flower, O son-in-law...

Son-in-law: She roams from that lane to this lane and tells me to cook for her, O mother-in-law... she keeps pestering me, O mother-in-law... Mother-in-law: You dried-up-faced fellow, O son-in-law... cook the rice without draining off the starch, O son-in-law... then my daughter will stay strong, O son-in-law...

Son-in-law: All the curry I cook, O mother-in-law... she gobbles it up like ripe fruit, O mother-in-law... Mother-in-law: Have you no sense, O son-in-law... can't you mix it and feed her by the mouthful, O son-in-law...

(Mother-in-law, O mother-in-law, your daughter is a whole basket of nagging, O mother-in-law, she's a whole basket of quarrels, my mother-in-law) (What is it, son-in-law, what's the matter, why are you saying such things, what's the matter, why are you saying such things, what's the matter)

Verse 2: Son-in-law: Look here... the pots are clattering, O mother-in-law... she sits peeling things and popping them into her mouth, O mother-in-law... she tells me to pick the lice from her hair, my mother-in-law... Mother-in-law: You dried-up-faced fellow, O son-in-law... she's only a tender green thing, O son-in-law... couldn't you give her a little something, O son-in-law...

Son-in-law: In front of my own people, O mother-in-law... she makes me look small, O mother-in-law... how am I to get by, O mother-in-law... Mother-in-law: How am I to tell her, O son-in-law... I'm only your aunt, after all, O son-in-law... how could I open my mouth, O son-in-law...

Son-in-law: Though I do every last bit of the drudgery, O mother-in-law... she won't show me any affection, look, mother-in-law... Mother-in-law: You with rats nesting in your eaves, O son-in-law... perhaps my daughter can't bear to look at you...

Son-in-law: Into the bathroom, O mother-in-law... she tells me to bring her water, O mother-in-law... tells me to bring her petticoat and blouse, my mother-in-law... Mother-in-law: How else am I to say it, O son-in-law... couldn't you scrub my daughter's back as well, O son-in-law... couldn't you rub a little soap on her too, O son-in-law...

Son-in-law: All these women's chores, O mother-in-law... why does your daughter make me do them, mother-in-law... Mother-in-law: Didn't you give her the upper hand, O son-in-law... so now keep your head down and stay meek, O son-in-law...

Son-in-law: This one, with a head as big as a basket, O mother-in-law... says her head is aching, O mother-in-law... and look, she calls me 'grandpa', mother-in-law... Mother-in-law: You grimy-faced fellow, O son-in-law... one look at your face, O son-in-law... and my daughter gets fed up, O son-in-law...

Son-in-law: Though I do every last bit of the drudgery, O mother-in-law... she won't show me any affection, look, mother-in-law... Mother-in-law: You with rats nesting in your eaves, O son-in-law... perhaps my daughter can't bear to look at you...

summaryEn:
A humorous duet between an alludu (son-in-law) and his atta (mother-in-law). The husband comes to complain about his wife: she roams the neighbourhood while he scrubs the dishes, sweeps the yard, cooks, fetches her bath water and her clothes, and even picks lice from her hair — yet she shames him in front of his own people and won't show him any affection. The mother-in-law answers every grievance by taking her daughter's side and mocking him instead. Her daughter grew up like a flower, she says; he should cook the rice without draining the starch, feed her by hand and scrub her back, and if his wife can't stand the sight of him, it's his own dried-up, grimy face that is to blame.

The comedy rests on turning household roles upside down, with the man stuck doing what he calls 'women's chores'. The refrain calling the wife a 'basket of quarrels' returns between the verses, and each exchange is built on the repeated calls 'O yatta' and 'O alluda'. At one point the mother-in-law seems to call herself his aunt, which may hint at the common custom of marrying within the family.
summaryTe:
ఇది అల్లుడు, అత్త మధ్య సాగే హాస్య యుగళగీతం. అల్లుడు తన భార్య గురించి అత్తకు ఫిర్యాదు చేస్తాడు: ఆమె ఊరంతా తిరుగుతుంటే తాను అంట్లు తోమాలి, వాకిలి ఊడ్వాలి, వంట చేయాలి, స్నానానికి నీళ్లు, లంగా రైకలు తెచ్చివ్వాలి, పేన్లు కూడా చూడాలి; అయినా తన వాళ్ల ముందే చులకన చేస్తుంది, తనతో సరసంగా ఉండదు అని వాపోతాడు. అత్త మాత్రం ప్రతి ఫిర్యాదుకూ బిడ్డ వైపే నిలబడి అల్లుడినే ఎగతాళి చేస్తుంది. తన బిడ్డ పువ్వులా పెరిగిందని, గంజి వంచకుండా అన్నం వండమని, ముద్దలు కలిపి తినిపించమని, వీపు రుద్దమని సలహాలిస్తుంది; బిడ్డ విసుగు పడుతోందంటే అది అల్లుడి ఎండిన, మాసిన మొహం వల్లేనని దెప్పిపొడుస్తుంది.

ఇంటి పనుల్లో ఆడ, మగ పాత్రలు తారుమారవడమే ఈ పాటలోని హాస్యానికి మూలం; అల్లుడు తాను చేస్తున్నవి ‘ఆడంగి పనులు’ అని బాధపడతాడు. భార్యను ‘గయ్యాలి గంప, కయ్యాల గంప’ అనే పల్లవి చరణాల మధ్య మళ్లీ మళ్లీ వస్తుంది, ‘ఓ యత్తా’, ‘ఓ అల్లుడా’ అనే పిలుపులతో ప్రతి సంభాషణ నడుస్తుంది. ఒక చోట అత్త తనను ‘మేనత్త’గా చెప్పుకున్నట్టు కనిపిస్తుంది, ఇది కుటుంబంలోనే పెళ్లిళ్లు చేసుకునే ఆచారాన్ని సూచిస్తుండవచ్చు.
